questions.question: What is the expected major product when Benzaldehyde is treated with Sodium borohydride (NaBH4) in ethanol?
questions.explanation: Treating Benzaldehyde with Sodium borohydride (NaBH4) in ethanol yields Benzyl alcohol. Rationale: NaBH4 selectively reduces aldehydes and ketones to alcohols without affecting esters, amides, or acids.

questions.question: Which reagent or set of reaction conditions will best accomplish the transformation of Methyl benzoate into Benzyl alcohol + Methanol?
questions.explanation: To convert Methyl benzoate into Benzyl alcohol + Methanol, the appropriate reagent is 1. LiAlH4 in ether; 2. Aqueous H3O+. Rationale: Powerful LiAlH4 reduces esters to primary alcohols through an aldehyde intermediate.

questions.question: What is the expected major product when Cyclohexylmagnesium bromide is treated with 1. Formaldehyde (HCHO); 2. H3O+?
questions.explanation: Treating Cyclohexylmagnesium bromide with 1. Formaldehyde (HCHO); 2. H3O+ yields Cyclohexylmethanol (primary alcohol). Rationale: Grignard attack on formaldehyde adds a single hydroxymethyl (-CH2OH) carbon unit.

questions.question: Which reagent or set of reaction conditions will best accomplish the transformation of Phenylmagnesium bromide into 1-Phenylethanol (secondary alcohol)?
questions.explanation: To convert Phenylmagnesium bromide into 1-Phenylethanol (secondary alcohol), the appropriate reagent is 1. Acetaldehyde (CH3CHO); 2. H3O+. Rationale: Nucleophilic addition of aryl Grignard to an aldehyde generates a secondary alcohol.

questions.question: What is the expected major product when Methylmagnesium bromide is treated with 1. Acetone ((CH3)2CO); 2. H3O+?
questions.explanation: Treating Methylmagnesium bromide with 1. Acetone ((CH3)2CO); 2. H3O+ yields 2-Methyl-2-propanol (tert-butanol, tertiary alcohol). Rationale: Nucleophilic addition of methyl Grignard to a ketone constructs a tertiary alcohol.

questions.topic: Selective oxidation of 1° alcohol to aldehyde
questions.question: Which reagent or set of reaction conditions will best accomplish the transformation of 1-Hexanol into Hexanal?
questions.explanation: To convert 1-Hexanol into Hexanal, the appropriate reagent is PCC (pyridinium chlorochromate) in CH2Cl2. Rationale: Anhydrous PCC oxidizes primary alcohols to aldehydes without over-oxidation to carboxylic acids.

questions.topic: Exhaustive oxidation of 1° alcohol to carboxylic acid
questions.question: Which starting material will react with CrO3 / aqueous H2SO4 (Jones reagent) to yield Hexanoic acid as the major product?
questions.explanation: 1-Hexanol reacts with CrO3 / aqueous H2SO4 (Jones reagent) to yield Hexanoic acid. Rationale: Hydrated aldehyde intermediate is rapidly oxidized by aqueous chromium(VI) to carboxylic acid.

questions.question: What is the expected major product when 2,3-Dimethyl-2,3-butanediol (pinacol) is treated with Concentrated H2SO4 / heat?
questions.explanation: Treating 2,3-Dimethyl-2,3-butanediol (pinacol) with Concentrated H2SO4 / heat yields 3,3-Dimethyl-2-butanone (pinacolone) + H2O. Rationale: Protonation, loss of water to form 3° carbocation, and 1,2-methyl shift driven by carbonyl resonance.

questions.question: Which starting material will react with 1. CO2 (125°C, 100 atm); 2. Aqueous HCl to yield Salicylic acid (2-hydroxybenzoic acid) as the major product?
questions.explanation: Sodium phenoxide reacts with 1. CO2 (125°C, 100 atm); 2. Aqueous HCl to yield Salicylic acid (2-hydroxybenzoic acid). Rationale: Phenoxide nucleophile attacks CO2 ortho to the hydroxyl group under high pressure.

questions.question: What is the expected major product when 1,4-Benzenediol (hydroquinone) is treated with Na2Cr2O7 / H2SO4?
questions.explanation: Treating 1,4-Benzenediol (hydroquinone) with Na2Cr2O7 / H2SO4 yields 1,4-Benzoquinone. Rationale: Oxidation of 1,4-hydroquinone removes two electrons and two protons to form the fully conjugated 1,4-dione.
